O*NET51-6052.00 covers garment design and making, alteration and repair, and fit adjustment. It does not merge assembly-line sewing, fashion creativity, metal templates, or bookbinding machines into a single occupation.

Inputs are client measurements and requirements, garment structure and materials, style or pattern, and craftsmanship requirements; body measurement information and finished-product specifications are kept separate, and shrinkage, direction, and tolerance that are not given cannot be decided on your own.

Take and record body or garment measurements, observe during fittings which areas need alteration, and communicate with the client about style and materials; the editorial suggestion is to keep confirmed and unconfirmed items separate.

Outputs are custom-made or repaired garments, patterns and cut pieces, and alteration records; actual measurements, appearance, and fit must be checked, and completing a drawing or order does not mean the garment passes acceptance.

Tailors can undo seams, let out or take in seams, adjust hems, mend, and replace pockets, zippers, buttons, and linings; first check the original garment's structure and available alteration allowance, and do not promise that all damage can be restored.

Lay out and cut per the pattern, baste and assemble, and sew, maintaining drape and proportion; real machine, needle, and shear operation requires instruction, and operating ability is not gained from paper problems.

Pressing is checked against the material and craftsmanship, and after completion the quality items such as measurements, appearance, stitching, and stray needles are checked; the standard gives task capability and does not provide a uniform temperature or result guarantee for every garment.
